subject: Post-call recap — Redwood integration & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Carter <alex.carter@acme.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap — Redwood integration & next steps

Hi Alex —

Thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we can keep momentum on the pilot. High-level notes below: feel free to correct anything I missed.

What we heard (pain points)
- Search relevance for support articles is inconsistent — current embedding + BM25 hybrid is missing context for short queries.
- Tail latency on peak (p95) spikes to 450–600ms which hurts UX for live chat.
- Unit cost is a concern — you want predictable per-request economics as traffic scales.
- Security/compliance: SOC 2 and data residency are must-haves for vendor selection.

Goals (agreed)
- Improve relevance for short queries (goal: +10–15% click-through on suggested articles).
- Reduce p95 inference latency to under 150ms for the chat use case (initial target for streaming path).
- Establish a 3-week pilot using production-ish data to measure latency, cost, and relevance.

Integration / product fit notes
- SDK changes: the Redwood SDK now supports client-side streaming (chunked token delivery) and built-in function calling helpers for structured outputs. This will let you stream partial answers into the UI while also invoking deterministic enrichment functions (e.g., fetch-ticket-metadata) for structured fields.
- Streaming vs non-streaming: streaming reduces perceived latency and helps p50 dramatically; tail improvements depend on batching and cache hit rates.
- Embeddings & reranking: recommend a two-stage pipeline — dense embeddings for candidate retrieval, then model-based reranker with a short context window for final ranking. We can provide pre-built reranker prompts and eval harness.
- Security: Redwood supports SOC 2, customer-managed KMS in Private deployments, and VPC peering for Dedicated.

Proposed pilot plan (3 weeks)
1) Week 0: Access & baseline — Redwood provides API keys (+ trial credits). Acme shares a deidentified sample of ~50k queries + doc corpus. (Owner: Acme — Alex)
2) Week 1: Integration & smoke tests — Dev integrates SDK streaming and embeddings endpoint; Redwood SE runs initial embedding/index build. (Owners: Dev + Rishi)
3) Week 2: Benchmarking & tuning — joint runs for latency, reranking evals, and cost profiling; iterate on quantization/batching config. (Owners: Rishi + Dev)
4) Week 3: Results & decision — present outcomes (latency, cost, relevance) and recommend next steps (Hosted -> Dedicated). (Owner: Marissa)

Action items / next steps
- Alex: Share deidentified sample dataset and procurement timeline (target this week).
- Dev: Confirm which frontend client will consume streaming (web socket vs SSE) and any platform constraints.
- Rishi: Prepare an initial arch diagram and security summary for your security team.

Attachments: redwood-integration-outline.pdf (integration checklist + milestones)

I'll follow up with a calendar invite for a technical sync with Rishi and Dev. Looking forward to the pilot — excited to see what we can improve for Acme.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>

Hi Alex — quick technical answers and attachments for your security team.

- SOC 2 & security: attaching a short security-summary.pdf covering SOC 2 scope, data handling, and KMS options. For Dedicated/Private we support customer-managed KMS + audit logs; Hosted can be isolated via org-level projects.
- Streaming latency: in our internal tests (on A100-class hardware with continuous batching) streaming reduced perceived p50 from ~220ms to ~80ms for interactive chat. p95 improvement depends on batching and KV cache hit rates — typical p95 we see for streaming chat setups is ~120–180ms; non-streaming p95s are often 2–3x higher under burst. We'll run an Acme-specific benchmark during Week 1 to give you exact numbers for your 1k/8k contexts.
- Embeddings/reranking: recommended flow — dense retrieval (512-d vectors) -> candidate set of 50 -> model reranker with 2–4 prompt examples. Reranker can be hosted as a lower-cost tuned model; we'll provide starter prompts and an eval harness.
- Cost during pilot: Redwood provides trial credits to cover API calls and indexing up to a reasonable cap; embedding indexing is billed based on vector count and storage during Dedicated. We'll surface an estimated cost sheet after baseline runs.

Attachments (included): redwood-arch-diagram.pdf (system architecture + recommended routing for streaming + dedicated fallbacks)
security-summary.pdf (SOC 2 scope, KMS options, data flow diagram)

Telemetry we’ll need:
- Request IDs (X-Request-ID) and timestamped logs for any latency anomalies
- Sample query IDs for failed/low-relevance examples
- Basic throughput numbers (requests/sec) during your peak windows

Proposed times for technical sync with SEs:
- Mon 9 Mar, 10:00–10:30 PT
- Tue 10 Mar, 14:00–14:30 PT

If either of those works for you I’ll send a calendar invite and include a short demo showing streaming + function calling in action.

Cheers,
